result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/design/REQ-030.md: walk-in registration at the door, with in-flow consent, phone-based person matching, and a logged capacity override -- the third and final Phase 6 requirement.

SCHEMA CHECK (Sec0, mandatory pre-check) -- NO CHANGE NEEDED, confirmed by direct inspection of db/schema.ts: users.tgId is nullable with a uniqueIndex that already treats every NULL as distinct (REQ-010, the exact property a walk-in User with no Telegram identity needs); profiles' six required columns are already nullable (REQ-019-schema.md); uq_registrations_event_user (unique on event_id+user_id) already exists, load-bearing for the insert-if-absent/update-if-present write shape. DATA-DESIGNER does not run this cycle.

INTERACTION PATTERN (Sec1) -- resolved explicitly, per the task's own steer. A single command captures all three fields (/walkin <event_id> <name>|<company>|<phone>), matching REQ-028's stateless-command precedent. The genuinely new piece: the requirement needs a confirm/cancel step BETWEEN data entry and storage (AC1), which neither REQ-019's DB-derived-resumability trick (unavailable -- S1 forbids writing anything, even a first partial row, before consent) nor REQ-028's single-shot command (no confirm step at all) can supply. Resolved as a genuinely stateless mechanism, not new state infrastructure: the confirm/override messages carry their own state AS THE BOT'S OWN MESSAGE TEXT (canonical Name:/Company:/Phone: labeled lines), re-parsed by the tap handler from ctx.callbackQuery.message.text -- never callback_data (ruled out on a hard technical constraint, Sec1.2: a UUID eventId alone already consumes 51 of the 64-byte callback_data budget, leaving no room for three free-text fields), never an in-memory map (S9's forbidden pattern), never a new DB column. Nothing is lost on a bot restart because nothing is held anywhere the bot's process or DB owns -- the carrier is the Telegram message itself, already displaying to the organizer the exact values they typed. AC1 becomes structurally true: the command handler performs zero writes; only a Confirm tap can ever reach the write function.

PERSON-MATCHING RULE (Sec3) -- phone-based, via a NEW getUserIdByPhone (domain/user.ts), matched against a digit-only normalization (normalizePhoneForMatching: strip every non-digit character, stated as prose not code). Explicitly justifies why not a country-aware canonicalization (this codebase spans 4+ countries' dialing conventions with no existing phone-parsing library) and states the tradeoff table: false negatives (same person, differently formatted numbers, e.g. missing country code) silently create a duplicate profile -- accepted as the cheaper failure mode; false positives require literal phone number reuse across two different people -- rare, not specific to this normalization. Matching only ever succeeds against a profile with a non-null phone already on file.

ATOMIC WRITE (Sec6) -- a NEW commitWalkin (domain/walkin.ts), called from BOTH the confirm tap (overrideConfirmed:false) and, only when needed, the override tap (overrideConfirmed:true) -- each its own transaction with a fresh locked read of the event and the (event,user) registration row, never trusting a value from an earlier tap (same S7 discipline toggleCheckIn/performQrCheckIn/overrideAdmitAndCheckIn already establish). A NEW pure decideWalkinOutcome (domain/walkin.ts) is a 7-row first-match-wins table covering event-not-ready/cancelled/finished, already-checked-in, check-in-existing-admitted (a pre-registered admitted person walking in needs only a check-in, no override), and admit-and-check-in vs. needs-override-confirmation (gated on seatsLeft>0 OR overrideConfirmed). Explicitly reasons why an existing waitlisted/requested/withdrawn/rejected registration is treated identically to 'no registration at all' for override purposes -- same reasoning REQ-029 Sec4's decideOverrideOutcome already applies to the QR-refusal path, applied here to the door (the requirement text's own pointer to reuse-or-design-a-variant). One INSERT/UPDATE + exactly one writeAuditLog call per outcome, action name selected by a table (registration.walkin_admit vs. registration.walkin_override_admit based on seatsLeft at write time) -- satisfies AC3's 'exactly one audit_log row' by the same one-transaction-one-write-one-audit discipline every other mutation in registration.ts already follows.

OVERRIDE STEP REUSES THE SAME STATELESS MECHANISM (Sec1.3) -- no placeholder registration row is ever written just to hand an id to a second callback (which would need its own dismiss-deletes-the-row bookkeeping). The override-offer message re-renders the SAME canonical Name:/Company:/Phone: lines; the override tap re-runs commitWalkin a second time -- safe because the person-matching resolve/create step (Sec6.2 point 3) is idempotent (a second call finds the just-created row by phone).

AUTHORIZATION (Sec4/Sec8) -- requireOrganizerForChapter (REQ-016, reused byte-for-byte unchanged), never requireEventStaffForEvent -- reasoned via S2 exactly as REQ-029's own override gate: EventStaff's rights are check-in-only, admitting past capacity is an organizer decision. Re-run at THREE separate points (the command, the confirm tap, the override tap), never trusted from an earlier check -- this triple-check is what makes AC6 provable at every entry point a stale button could reach.

S11 (Sec10) -- every writeAuditLog payload in this design is a fixed shape ({eventId, previousAdmission, source}) that structurally never includes phone; no log.* call anywhere in the new handlers receives the phone value. Explicitly distinguishes the one place phone IS shown (the confirm/stale-message reply, echoed back into the SAME chat the organizer just typed it into) from S11's negative case (logs/audit/third-party), citing REQ-019 Sec2.5's identical no-third-party-exposure reasoning.

All 6 ACs mapped to concrete design elements in Sec11. 6 open questions stated explicitly in Sec12: whether company should be a hard-required door field (design treats only name/phone as required); whether a phone match should update the existing profile's stale name/company (design leaves it untouched); whether a User/Profile created ahead of a since-dismissed override should be rolled back (design leaves it committed -- AC3 only forbids the registration row surviving); the new user's chapterId defaulting to the event's chapter (untested convenience default); the whole door name string going into first_name with no first/last split; the Event: line in the canonical message being unverified against the tapped button's eventId (a residual, no-AC-exercised gap, not silently assumed closed).
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 1b) -- DATA-DESIGNER does not run this cycle, no stored-data change (users.tgId nullable+uniqueIndex, profiles' relaxed NOT NULLs, uq_registrations_event_user, chk_registrations_checked_in_only_if_admitted all pre-exist from prior requirements). Note for CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR: verify the message-text-re-parse mechanism (Sec1/Sec7) is read as a genuinely stateless pattern (the carrier is a Telegram-held message, not bot-process or DB state) rather than a disguised conversation-state violation of the REQ-019/REQ-028 precedent it explicitly distinguishes itself from.
